# Commands

Every build, run and test command across webos-phoenix, phoenix-ember-glass-ui (the 2.0 shell), phoenix-default-apps and ember-glass-ui, checked against the scripts themselves. Each command is its own code block, so GitHub's copy button copies just that command. For a searchable page with a Mac/Linux filter, run `python3 tools/commands-doc.py --html build/commands.html` and open it in a browser.

| Repo | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| webos-phoenix | 1.0: the shell, the simulator, the original apps |
| phoenix-ember-glass-ui | 2.0: webos-phoenix with the Ember Glass shell |
| phoenix-default-apps | the rebuilt built-in apps |
| ember-glass-ui | the 2.0 UI layer the apps use |

## Get the code

phoenix-ember-glass-ui is webos-phoenix with the 2.0 shell: it takes 1.0's changes by merging webos-phoenix's main. The default apps build against the webos-phoenix commit named in `phoenix-default-apps/phoenix.pin.json`. Ember Glass checks its facade against phoenix-default-apps (`tools/facade-check/facade/SOURCE.json`). The 2.0 shell carries a copy of Ember Glass's tokens (`shell/qml/Phoenix/Shell/EmberGlass.qml`).

### Clone webOS Phoenix with its submodules

Run in `parent folder` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:116`

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/thebestbradley/webos-phoenix.git && cd webos-phoenix
```

### Clone the private repos beside it

They need your GitHub sign-in (a credential helper or an SSH key). The tools look for `../webos-phoenix` and `../phoenix-default-apps`.

Run in `parent folder of webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `phoenix-default-apps/tools/lib/phoenix.mjs:30 · ember-glass-ui/tools/facade-check.mjs:17`

The rebuilt built-in apps:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/thebestbradley/phoenix-default-apps.git
```

The 2.0 UI layer the apps use:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/thebestbradley/ember-glass-ui.git
```

The 2.0 shell:

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/thebestbradley/phoenix-ember-glass-ui.git
```

### Fetch the submodules

The original Open webOS apps in `third_party/`. `./phoenix` does this too.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/CLAUDE.md:41 · phoenix:474`

```sh
git submodule update --init
```

### Update to the latest main

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:122`

```sh
git checkout main && git pull && git submodule update --init
```

### Bring 1.0's changes into the 2.0 shell

Run in `phoenix-ember-glass-ui` · Mac + Linux · Source: `phoenix-ember-glass-ui/docs/SYSTEM-UI-2.md`

Once:

```sh
git remote add upstream https://github.com/thebestbradley/webos-phoenix.git
```

```sh
git fetch upstream && git merge upstream/main && git submodule update --init
```

## Set up a Mac

### See what's installed and what's missing

A dry run: it changes nothing.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:31`

```sh
./phoenix check
```

### Install everything and build

One command installs Xcode's command line tools, Homebrew, Qt, CMake, Ninja, Node 22, Python 3.12, PHP and the assistant's programs and models, then builds.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:9-10,41-48 · docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:135-144`

Install what's missing, then build:

```sh
./phoenix
```

Also the test tools: Playwright, plus Radicale, WsgiDAV, Pillow and NumPy in .venv:

```sh
./phoenix --tests
```

Skip the assistant's models and its two Homebrew packages:

```sh
./phoenix --no-assistant
```

Download nothing:

```sh
./phoenix --offline
```

Install without building:

```sh
./phoenix setup
```

Show what it would do:

```sh
./phoenix --dry-run
```

```sh
./phoenix --help
```

### Put Node 22 on the PATH for new terminals

Run in `any folder` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:155`

```sh
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zprofile
```

### Turn on the Python test packages

Once per terminal, before the DAV, backup and HiDPI tests.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:314-316`

```sh
source .venv/bin/activate
```

### Set up by hand instead

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:128,161-165`

```sh
xcode-select --install
```

```sh
brew install qt cmake ninja node@22
```

```sh
export PATH="$(brew --prefix)/opt/node@22/bin:$PATH"
```

```sh
git submodule update --init
```

```sh
cmake -S shell -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix qt)"
```

```sh
cmake --build build
```

### Optional extras

Run in `any folder` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:271 · docs/BUILDING-MAC.md:108`

To build the Flutter Notes demo:

```sh
brew install --cask flutter
```

For the ARM64 VM and the UTM bundles:

```sh

```

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/scripts/mac-setup.sh:10-19`

## Set up Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)

It asks for sudo. It installs apt packages, Qt 6.8.1 into `/opt/Qt`, Node 22, and builds `whisper-cli` and `llama-server` into `/usr/local/bin`.



```sh
./phoenix --no-assistant
```

### Install without building

For a cloud environment's setup script. The two lines do the same thing.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:374,377 · scripts/linux-setup.sh:48`

```sh
./phoenix setup --tests
```


Run in `webos-phoenix` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:378`

```sh

```

Lets the assistant's voice play into nothing.

Run in `any folder` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:288-290`

```sh
echo 'pcm.!default { type null }' > ~/.asoundrc
```

### Older wrapper script

It calls `./phoenix`, and takes `--tests`, `--deps` and `--no-assistant`.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/scripts/linux-setup.sh:16-25`

## Build

### Build

Incremental. `./phoenix build` is the same.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:9-10`

```sh
./phoenix
```

### Start the build over

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:387-400`

```sh
rm -rf build && ./phoenix
```

### Rebuild only the web apps

Run in `webos-phoenix/apps` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:401-403`

```sh
npm run build
```

### Build into another folder

Other overrides: `PHOENIX_QT_DIR` (a Qt 6.8 or newer), `QT_PREFIX` (Linux, default `/opt/Qt`), `CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL`.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:65-67`

```sh
PHOENIX_BUILD_DIR=build-other ./phoenix
```

### What ./phoenix runs for a new build folder

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:594,602`

**Mac:**:

```sh
cmake -S shell -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix qt)"
```

**Linux:**:

```sh
cmake -S shell -B build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/Qt/6.8.1/gcc_64
```

```sh
cmake --build build --parallel
```

### A release build without the npm step

CMake switches: `PHOENIX_BUILD_SIM`, `PHOENIX_BUILD_KEYBOARD` and `PHOENIX_BUILD_APPS`, all on by default.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/CMakeLists.txt:11,49,164 · .github/workflows/ci.yml:156`

```sh
cmake -S shell -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPHOENIX_BUILD_APPS=OFF -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix qt)"
```

## Simulator: start

### Build if needed, then run

Adaptive is the default: the layout follows the window's size. Everything after the mode goes to phoenix-sim.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/phoenix:11-15 · README.md:226-229`

Adaptive:

```sh
./phoenix run
```

```sh
./phoenix run phone
```

```sh
./phoenix run tablet
```

```sh
./phoenix run tablet --scene cards
```

Show the command it would run:

```sh
./phoenix run --dry-run tablet
```

### Run without building

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:175,185`

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim
```

Every option:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --help
```

### Start as a new device

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/main.cpp:189,225-256 · CLAUDE.md:73`

Run First Use again:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --first-use
```

Another device with its own data: a clean start on a Mac too; delete its phoenix-sim-try1 folder after:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --tablet --instance try1
```

**Linux:** A fresh home folder: a clean device (documented for Linux):

```sh
HOME=$(mktemp -d) ./build/phoenix-sim --tablet
```

### Run two simulators at once

Each `--instance` is a device of its own: its own data, installed apps, web storage and settings. Without it, two simulators would share one device and one web storage. Each one's **Window** menu lists every simulator running for you, from any checkout or build (its layout and size, look and checkout), and brings the one you choose to the front; **Next Simulator** (Ctrl+Shift+\) goes to the next.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/main.cpp:225-256,733-766 · shell/sim/siminstances.h · shell/sim/simchrome.cpp:572-729 · docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:227-250`

1.0:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --tablet --instance v1
```

in `phoenix-ember-glass-ui`: 2.0, with the rebuilt apps:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --tablet --instance v2 --extra-rootfs ../phoenix-default-apps/build/rootfs -- --look ember-glass
```

### Run without a display

SSH sessions and containers. `./phoenix run` does this itself when xvfb-run is installed.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:305-306 · phoenix:638-650`

```sh
QTWEBENGINE_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1 xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1200x24" ./build/phoenix-sim --tablet --scene cards --screenshot out.png
```

### Choose the open app to view

The menu bar's **Window** menu lists the simulators running on this computer first (as in Run two simulators at once), then the open cards, in card view's order with the windows stacked on a card under it, and brings the one you choose to the front, maximized; a check mark is on the card in front. It also has Card View, Launcher, Next Card (Ctrl+Shift+], ⇧⌘] on a Mac) and Previous Card (Ctrl+Shift+[). Locked, the card chosen is the one in front once you unlock.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/simchrome.cpp:272-286,499-570,731-749 · shell/qml/Phoenix/Sim/SimWindowMenu.qml · shell/qml/sim.qml:901-911`

```sh

```

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/main.cpp:201-224`



### Services and the assistant

Also: `--host-shell PATH`, `--no-tcp-relay`, `--llama-server PATH`, `--speech-command CMD`, `--wake-model DIR`, `--vosk-library FILE`, `--wake-file FILE`, `--qml-dir DIR`, `--repo-dir DIR`. Environment: `PHOENIX_WHISPER_CLI`, `PHOENIX_WHISPER_MODEL`, `PHOENIX_TTS_PROGRAM`.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/main.cpp:192-193,206-216 · README.md:357-358`

Start the catalog and open the Marketplace:

```sh
./phoenix run --marketplace
```

No catalog this run:

```sh
./phoenix run --no-marketplace
```

The Terminal app gets no shell on your computer:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --no-host-shell
```

WAV files as the microphone, in turn:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --microphone-file call.wav --microphone-file yes.wav
```

### Without a GPU

The shell tells by the renderer whether a GPU draws, and prints it (`phoenix: renderer ...`). Without one it leaves out the blur behind translucent surfaces, as it always did with Qt Quick's software renderer: also for OpenGL or Vulkan on a software rasteriser such as Mesa's llvmpipe (a VM, a container, a board without its GPU driver). `PHOENIX_SOFTWARE_RENDERING` (`1`, `0` or `auto`) does the same on a device.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/shell/sim/main.cpp:227,300-309 · shell/native/renderinfo.h`

As without a GPU: no blur:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --software-rendering on
```

The blur, even on a software rasteriser:

```sh
./build/phoenix-sim --software-rendering off
```

The same through the environment:

```sh
PHOENIX_SOFTWARE_RENDERING=1 ./build/phoenix-sim
```

## Test: shell

### Point QMLTEST at Qt's test runner

Once per terminal.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/CLAUDE.md:80-81 · docs/GETTING-STARTED.md:328-330`

**Mac:**:

```sh
export QMLTEST="$(brew --prefix qt)/bin/qmltestrunner"
```

**Linux:**:

```sh
export QMLTEST=/opt/Qt/6.8.1/gcc_64/bin/qmltestrunner
```

### Run the QML tests

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/.github/workflows/ci.yml:180,487-497 · README.md:465`

**Mac:** All of them, as CI runs them on the Mac (offscreen Metal stalls animations):

```sh
QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen "$QMLTEST" -import shell/qml -import build/qml -input shell/tests
```

**Linux:** All of them:

```sh
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen "$QMLTEST" -import shell/qml -import build/qml -input shell/tests
```

One file:

```sh
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen "$QMLTEST" -import shell/qml -import build/qml -input shell/tests/tst_launcher.qml
```

The device shell over fake modules:

```sh
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen "$QMLTEST" -import shell/qml -import build/qml -import shell/tests-device/fakes -input shell/tests-device
```

HiDPI at 2x:

```sh
QT_SCALE_FACTOR=2 QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen "$QMLTEST" -import shell/qml -import build/qml -input shell/tests/tst_hidpi.qml
```

## Device images and VMs

### Parse check

About 12 minutes per machine, not as root. `PHOENIX_PARSE_DIR`, `PHOENIX_PARSE_TARGET` and `PHOENIX_PARSE_COMPRESS` adjust it.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/scripts/parse-check.sh:8,22-36 · docs/HARDWARE.md:1672-1683`


```sh
scripts/parse-check.sh
```

```sh
scripts/parse-check.sh fairphone-fp6 phoenix-vm-arm64
```

When you are root:


Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor blocks BitBake otherwise (CI does this on a throwaway machine):

```sh

```

### Run the ARM64 VM as a device

QEMU 8.2 or later. HVF on Apple silicon, KVM on an ARM64 Linux host, emulation otherwise. Ctrl+A X quits. Options: `--image PATH` `--kernel FILE` `--cpus N` `--memory MIB` `--cap-cpu PCT` `--gl on|off` `--audio virtio|hda|none` `--display SPEC` `--accel hvf|kvm|tcg` `--ssh-port N` `--fresh` and `-- <QEMU options>`.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/scripts/vm.sh:11-44,240,260 · docs/BUILDING-MAC.md:97-131`


```sh
scripts/vm.sh fairphone-fp6
```

Show the QEMU command:

```sh
scripts/vm.sh fairphone-fp6 --dry-run
```

Into the running VM:

```sh
ssh -p 2222 root@127.0.0.1
```

in `inside the VM`: Inside the VM: which device it became:

```sh
journalctl -u phoenix-device-select
```

in `inside the VM`: Boot time:

```sh
systemd-analyze
```

in `inside the VM`: Collect logs:

```sh
phoenix-diag
```

## Local servers

### Marketplace catalog

PHP 8 with sodium and pdo_sqlite, on port 8088. One for every simulator of every checkout, in `~/.local/share/phoenix/catalog` (on a Mac `~/Library/Application Support/Phoenix/catalog`; `MARKETPLACE_DATA` elsewhere; the first start imports a checkout's old `server/marketplace/data`). The simulator starts it itself, and it runs while any simulator does; `serve.sh` by hand serves until stopped (`--no-fill`: without filling itself). Its review page is `/admin`; the token is `admin.token` in that folder. `availability` turns kinds of app, feeds and apps on or off per device class (docs/APP-STORE.md 3.17).

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/server/marketplace/bin/serve.sh:9-16,35-43,135-185 · bin/marketplace.php:43-52,207-245 · README.md "On this computer (for now)", "Device classes and kinds"`

```sh
server/marketplace/bin/serve.sh
```

Also init, publish, admin, queue, approve, reject, key, developer, versions:

```sh
php server/marketplace/bin/marketplace.php seed
```

--phoenix for a Phoenix app, with --listing LISTING.json:

```sh
php server/marketplace/bin/marketplace.php upload FILE.ipk
```

What is on where: also on, feed NAME, app ID classes CLASS,..., app ID kind KIND; alone, prints it:

```sh
php server/marketplace/bin/marketplace.php availability off kind legacy phone
```

```sh
python3 server/marketplace/bin/probe-pwas.py
```

### The Marketplace's hosted apps

Open-source web apps from their upstreams' releases (pinned in `server/marketplace/catalog/web-apps.json`; docs/WEB-APP-CATALOG.md), and the 2.0 apps from a phoenix-default-apps checkout (`--from` or `PHOENIX_DEFAULT_APPS`; skipped without one). Downloads go to a cache outside the repository (`--cache`, `PHOENIX_WEB_APPS_CACHE`). `--software-gl` for WebGL 2 apps on a machine without a GPU.

Run in `webos-phoenix` · Mac + Linux · Source: `webos-phoenix/server/marketplace/bin/web-apps.py:28-58,738-975 · bin/marketplace.php:26,177 · README.md "Open-source web apps and the 2.0 apps"`

## Gotchas

- `./phoenix run` uses up the first `--`: for the 2.0 look, write `./phoenix run phone -- -- --look ember-glass`.
- phoenix-sim has no `--terminal`. That flag belongs to `tools/serve-rootfs.py`; in the simulator it's `--no-host-shell` or `--host-shell PATH`.
- `ctest` finds nothing: run the C++ test programs by name.
- Without `PHOENIX_SIM`, phoenix-default-apps' `npm run sim` runs inside the webos-phoenix checkout, so a relative `--screenshot` file lands there.
- There's no run or flash script yet for the `qemux86-64` and Raspberry Pi images.
- For a clean device on a Mac, start with a new `--instance NAME`; on Linux a fresh `HOME` works too.
- The repos pin each other: `phoenix-default-apps/phoenix.pin.json` (the webos-phoenix commit), `ember-glass.pin.json` on its `ember-glass-preview` branch, ember-glass-ui's `tools/facade-check/facade/SOURCE.json`, and the 2.0 shell's copy of the tokens. Move a pin when the repo it names moves.
